object_description: large school volume composed of three assembled bodies
design_condition: The assembled volume is set within a wooded park and shaped around existing topography, creating multiple access levels and connections between the school and surrounding park spaces.

positive.statement: The large volume and cultural buildings create a convincing transition between town and countryside.
Existing topography and part of the tree heritage are conserved and adapted.
The three-courtyard organization provides two level access routes and connects the park's subspaces.
The three assembled bodies manage the large scale while providing covered transitions between exterior and interior.
Public functions are clearly legible and can operate independently outside school hours.
The sloping facade and patios provide simple circulation, varied daylight, and exterior views.
The articulated plan generates a strong classroom-floor typology with natural light and exterior views.
Horizontal circulation has almost urban spatial qualities and useful exterior clearances.
The landscape approach sensitively manages existing trees and runoff while diversifying planting.

negative.statement: Classrooms in the internal corners remain a weak point.
School access has too few stairs and undersized entrance halls for the number of users.
Some classroom corridors are too narrow.
The patios have an unfavorable width-to-height ratio.
The documentation center should be directly accessible from the media-library area.
An exterior terrace is needed for the refectory.
Club equipment rooms and student changing rooms are poorly related to the sports hall.
The northern parking arrangement makes sharing with the municipal program difficult.
Teaching rooms facing the avenue are highly exposed to road noise.
Some sustainability aspects require consolidation, despite good ventilation and sun protection.
